messages:
mari: hey team — mari here, first week on infra. trying to create a GKE cluster in project redwood-dev-apac but I hit a 403 when enabling the compute API and when attempting to link the billing account. error says: "Permission 'resourcemanager.projects.setBillingInfo' denied." who should I ping to get the org billing link or a temporary lift? also need an AWS assume role for staging (cross-account).

evant: welcome mari :wave:

evant: re: GCP billing error — that permission lives at the org/billingAccount level. we usually request billing links via the infra-requests form (https://redwood.internal/infra-requests) — can you paste the project id and the billing account id you want to attach? 

mari: project id is redwood-dev-apac, billing account looks like 0123-4567-8901. I tried gcloud billing projects link but got the same permission error.

lucy: cc @cloud-onboarding — if org policy blocks billing linkage we'll need finance to approve. two options: 1) infra team can link it if you file a request, 2) we can create a short-lived service account with billing.link permission and hand it to you (less preferred).

platform-oncall-bot: Note: There is an active org-level constraint 'constraints/iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation' that may impact some flows. Run `gcloud projects get-iam-policy redwood-dev-apac` to see current bindings.

mari: thanks — sharing the output of `gcloud projects get-iam-policy redwood-dev-apac` below:
```
bindings:
- members:
  - serviceAccount:project-org-admins@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com
  role: roles/billing.user
```

evant: that shows only the org admin SA can link billing. if you need immediate access for the cluster spin up, open the infra-requests form and pick "billing link request" with urgency "1-urgent" and include your cluster plan and why region asia-southeast1 is required. I'll route the request to finance.

tom: for the AWS piece — what permissions do you need? if it's cross-account assume we already have an ARN template: arn:aws:iam::999999999999:role/Redwood-Staging-Developer. send me your user ARN and I'll add a trust policy.

mari: I need sts:AssumeRole + S3 read for the staging bucket redwood-staging-artifacts. my AWS user is arn:aws:iam::123456789012:user/mari

lucy: tom — can you create the role with a time-limited session (90 days) and add mari as principal? we prefer short expirations for new hires.

tom: on it. I'll create the role and post the assume-role command. expect it in ~20m.

evant: mari — in parallel, please file the infra-requests entry and paste the request id here so I can escalate with finance (they're usually quick for onboarding). also add the cluster config (node count, machine type, expected QPS) so they can approve capacity and billing.

mari: filing now. request id IR-9876, urgency high, notes: GKE cluster redwood-dev-apac, region asia-southeast1, 3 n1-standard-8 nodes, will host canary traffic for staging.

platform-oncall-bot: Infra request IR-9876 received. Assigned to #infra-ops. ETA 4 business hours (may be faster).

mari: awesome — thanks everyone. appreciate the walkthrough.

tom: role created. Use the following to assume (sts token valid for 1h):
```
aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::999999999999:role/Redwood-Staging-Developer --role-session-name mari-onboard
```

lucy: once you confirm you can assume the role and link billing, reply here and we can mark this thread as resolved.

mari: confirmed — I could assume the role and the infra team linked the billing within an hour. cluster create succeeded. closing out, thanks :tada:
